summary.text: Brian Lawson is a Republican member of the South Carolina House of Representatives who represents District 30, having assumed office on November 14, 2022, and is seeking re-election in the general election on November 3, 2026.
Ballotpedia lists his profession as controller, and notes that the Republican primary for his seat was canceled.

paragraphs.text: Lawson was born in Spartanburg, South Carolina, and lives in Chesnee, South Carolina; he earned an A.S. from Columbia Southern University in 2022.
His career experience, according to Ballotpedia, includes working as a controller and as director of operations of American TransMed, Inc.

He has served on the board of directors of the South Carolina EMS Association, as president of the South Carolina Ambulance Providers Association, and on the board of directors of Cherokee County First Steps.
Lawson succeeded Steve Moss in the seat and is assigned to the Invitations and Memorial Resolutions Committee and the Labor, Commerce and Industry Committee in the 2025-2026 session.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he has lived in the Chesnee area of Cherokee County for twenty-two years and is a member of Arrowwood Baptist Church, where he serves as a deacon.
He listed his campaign's key messages as affordability for South Carolina families and support for first responders and veterans.
He said the issues he hears from residents include improving roads, strengthening infrastructure, keeping more money in residents' pockets, and less government.
